title: Killing Members of the Group
thesis: Track 2 MAID — created by Bill C-7 — is being applied to disabled, chronically ill, and economically vulnerable Canadians. Ontario's own Chief Coroner has documented Track 2 deaths driven by housing insecurity, poverty, and isolation, including patients with treatable conditions and untreated mental illness or addictions.

scenes.headline: Killing Members of the Group
scenes.subhead: The Ontario Chief Coroner's MAiD Death Review Committee documents the cases the federal government will not.

scenes.context: The Office of the Chief Coroner for Ontario published nine MDRC reports in 2024 reviewing complex MAID provisions, including Track 2 cases involving poverty, isolation, and untreated mental illness.

scenes.speaker: Office of the Chief Coroner of Ontario, MAiD Death Review Committee
scenes.quote: The Committee identified cases in which Track 2 MAiD was provided to persons whose suffering was substantially driven by unmet social needs — housing insecurity, poverty, isolation — rather than the medical condition cited as the grievous and irremediable basis for eligibility.

scenes.speaker: Ontario MAiD Death Review Committee — case review
scenes.speaker_meta: Track 2 case involving inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), 2023
scenes.quote: A patient with IBD, untreated mental illness, and active substance use was approved and provided MAiD on Track 2. The Committee found the assessment did not adequately explore reasonable treatment alternatives or address the contribution of unaddressed psychiatric and addiction-related suffering to the request.

scenes.context: Cumulative Ontario MAiD compliance reports flag procedural and substantive non-compliance — including inadequate exploration of alternatives, missing safeguards, and same-day approvals — affecting hundreds of provisions.

scenes.headline: Why this satisfies Article 6(a)
scenes.body:
The killing element is documented by the state itself. Ontario's Chief Coroner — a statutory office — has reviewed cases and concluded that Track 2 deaths are being driven by social conditions the federal government refuses to remedy. The group is identifiable: disabled, chronically ill, poor. The killing is administered by clinicians under a federal statute. The deaths are recorded in coroner files.

Article 6(a) does not require that the entire group be killed. It requires intent to destroy the group in whole or in part. Track 2 is the part.
